criteria.no: The item does not state it: it is silent about block_on, only uses other bridging such as spawn_blocking, or describes block_on calls outside the writer thread.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions block_on but whether it commits to the limit cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: The item states this limit on block_on in production code by one of these forms.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state that production code calls no block_on (Runtime::block_on, Handle::block_on or futures::executor::block_on) except Runtime::block_on on the SQLite writer's dedicated OS thread, as `anchor.statement` requires? Count an explicit statement of that limit, a statement that the writer thread's Runtime::block_on is the only block_on left, or the removal of a block_on call together with a statement that no block_on variant remains in the affected production code. Judge presence of this commitment only; do not judge conflict.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item conflicts: it complies, is silent, or uses only allowed mechanisms.
criteria.unclear: The item may plan such a call, but its details cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: The item plans such a production block_on call.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan production code that `anchor.statement` rules out? A conflict is any production call of Handle::block_on or futures::executor::block_on anywhere, including on the SQLite writer's own thread, or of Runtime::block_on anywhere other than the SQLite writer's dedicated OS thread (for example on reader threads, caller threads, CLI handlers or an application main). Not conflicts: Runtime::block_on on the writer's dedicated thread, block_on in #[cfg(test)] test code, blocking_recv, spawn_blocking, and silence about block_on. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item concerns something else, such as documentation of unrelated features, dependency versions, CI, or components with no sync/async bridging.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell whether it touches any of these.
criteria.yes: The item creates, changes or specifies one of these: block_on calls, runtime construction or entry points, the SQLite writer or reader threads, or a sync/async bridge.

relevant.instructions: Does the work described in `item.text` touch the area named in `anchor.scope`: async/blocking rules, any block_on call or Tokio runtime construction, the SQLite writer or its thread, the SQLite reader pool, or code that bridges synchronous and asynchronous code (sync wrappers over async calls, spawn_blocking, blocking_recv, async entry points, async test fixtures)? Judge subject overlap only; do not judge whether the item follows `anchor.statement`.
